hypothesis: Four independent per-thread accumulators should reduce the dependency chain in the input streaming loop while retaining the existing 1024-CTA, 256-thread grid-stride ownership. Fusing absolute value with each CTA's reduction also avoids materializing and rereading an n-element absolute-value array. The candidate is unmeasured; the supplied source does not contain a two-stage fused parent, so comparison with its measured baseline will not isolate the CTA mapping effect.
notes: The supplied baseline was correct with a 1.228 ms mean full-call time. This candidate keeps its input CTA/lane indexing, writes 1024 scratch partials, and uses one 256-thread CUB finalizer. No speedup is claimed; controller validation and full-call measurements are needed.
transformations: Fuse absolute value and CTA-local reduction, replacing the full-size absolute-value scratch pass with one partial per CTA.
Retain 1024 CTAs, 256 threads, and the existing grid-stride input ownership; use four independent accumulators per thread and guard all unrolled tail loads.
Reduce the fixed 1024 partials in one 256-thread CUB finalizer and write the result directly, avoiding floating-point atomics.
